_notes: Locally added -- upstream pinmame-nvram-maps has no map for Avatar.
Every address here was found by watching an automated 4-player game rather than by reading
values out of a capture: the ALP4K was driven through its own streamer, so nothing was typed in
off the display and nothing had to be trusted.
current_player and current_ball are adjacent bytes in CPU RAM at 0x000384A8 and 0x000384A9,
player low and ball high -- the shape every Stern SAM game checked uses. The player byte
completed 1->2->3 three times, once per ball; the ball byte once.
Scores are 4 bytes on 8-byte centres from 0x021109E4, the only group of four evenly spaced
values that rose monotonically through the game. Same base as 24, X-Men and twd_156c, and the
same 8-byte spacing as 24 -- but that is coincidence, not inheritance: the base and stride are
per-ROM across every SAM game measured.
player_count at 0x02110900, the one address shared by every SAM game checked.
High score records are 0x20 apart from 0x02102A38 with NUL-terminated initials at +0x00, a
4-byte score at +0x18 and a 16-bit checksum in the last two bytes of the first 30. Six records
pass that check and the seventh does not, which is what bounds the block.
The first five hold Stern's factory ladder (75M/55M/40M/30M/25M with 'G S'/'L R'/'J R'/'D T'/
'P P'). The sixth, 'LFS' at 25,000,000 and 0x02102AD8, is real -- its checksum validates -- but
what the machine calls it has not been read off its champion display, so it is left out of
mode_champions rather than guessed at. Its checksum region is still declared.
Only avr_200 is claimed; SAM addresses move between revisions.
